market.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (research/educational use; see docs/dataset_notes.md)

cutoff.decision_rule: A row for session t is decided at that session's timestamp (pre-open, 05:00 UTC in this series) and every feature uses bars up to and including t-1 only; values are computed at the close of their bar and shifted forward one row.
cutoff.news_cutoff_rule: news_cutoff_utc = session date at 00:00 UTC. Phase 4 may only use articles whose available_from is at or before it, i.e. day-precision news published on the previous day at the latest. Phase 3 reads no news at all.
cutoff.target: target = 1 when close[t] > close[t-1] for the predicted session t; next_session_return records the exact return it was derived from. No purge gap is needed because no row depends on another row's period.

definitions.return_1d: close[t-1] / close[t-1-1] - 1 (simple return over 1 session(s), known at close t-1)
definitions.return_5d: close[t-1] / close[t-1-5] - 1 (simple return over 5 session(s), known at close t-1)
definitions.return_20d: close[t-1] / close[t-1-20] - 1 (simple return over 20 session(s), known at close t-1)
definitions.sma_ratio_10: close[t-1] / mean(close[t-10 .. t-1]) - 1 at close t-1
definitions.sma_ratio_50: close[t-1] / mean(close[t-50 .. t-1]) - 1 at close t-1
definitions.rsi_14: Wilder RSI(14) on closes up to t-1
definitions.volatility_20: stdev(ddof=1) of simple returns over 20 sessions ending at t-1 (not annualised)
definitions.volume_ratio_20: volume[t-1] / mean(volume[t-20 .. t-1]) at close t-1

notes: 50 leading row(s) dropped: the indicators' warm-up window is not yet full; nothing was imputed
every feature is computed from bars up to and including t-1 and shifted forward one row, so session t itself cannot influence its own row (invariant 2)
target = 1 when the predicted session closes above the previous close; next_session_return is the exact return used to derive it
news_cutoff_utc = session date at 00:00 UTC; Phase 4 may only use articles whose available_from is at or before it (day-precision news published the day before at the latest)
no news data is read in Phase 3; this table is the market-only baseline's input

naive_majority.definition: always predict the majority class of the training period

comparison.note: A single held-out period of a few hundred sessions is a small sample: a difference of a few points is indistinguishable from noise. This result is a baseline measurement, not evidence of predictive skill or profitability.

limitations: One instrument (SPY) and one historical window: results do not generalise to other markets or periods.
Daily bars only; no intraday information, order flow, or after-hours prices.

Precision/recall/F1 describe the positive ('closes up') class; SPY's positive base rate is near 55%, so accuracy alone is misleading — balanced accuracy and the naive baseline are the fair comparison.
Hyper-parameter selection used a single validation period; with this few rows the selected C is itself noisy.
No news features are used yet (Phase 4); this is the market-only baseline the core research question compares against.
Transaction costs and execution are irrelevant here because no trading is simulated (Phase 5).
This is a research baseline, not financial advice, and it makes no claim of reliable prediction.
next_step: Phase 4 — aggregate pre-cutoff news into per-session features (counts by category, sentiment, no-news indicator) and train the same model family on the same splits to answer the research question.
